q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is August 20, 2026. NVIDIA is scheduled to report Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 — that's **6 days away**. This is an extremely short timeframe where the guidance is essentially already determined and will be announced imminently.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already issued explicit forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026:
- **$91.0 billion ± 2%**
- This creates a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion

This guidance was provided in their Q1 FY2027 earnings release. With earnings arriving in 6 days, it is highly unlikely NVIDIA will materially revise this guidance before announcing actual results. Companies rarely issue major guidance revisions mere days before earnings — it would signal either:
1. A significant miss to their own forward guidance (reputationally damaging)
2. An unexpected positive development (rare to change guidance this close to release)

The current research indicates wall street consensus is approximately $91.9 billion, which falls squarely within NVIDIA's stated guidance range.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Unexpected negative development** (unforeseen supply chain disruption, customer cancellation, geopolitical shock) — extremely unlikely with 6 days to announcement
- **Significant China revenue ban changes** affecting guidance assumptions — the guidance already assumes *zero* China datacenter compute revenue, so this wouldn't cause a downward revision
- **Major customer pullback or demand deterioration** — no evidence of this in the research provided

Realistically, downward revisions this close to earnings are rare without material negative news.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Better-than-expected demand** late in the quarter — possible but would more likely show up in actual Q2 results rather than forward guidance revision
- **Upside surprise in other segments** (Gaming, Professional Visualization) — again, more likely to affect Q2 actual results
- **China policy reversal** allowing datacenter compute sales — the guidance explicitly assumes zero from China, so a policy change could enable significant upside, but this seems unlikely in a 6-day window

Upward revisions this close to earnings are also uncommon, as guidance was set relatively recently (May 2026) and Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) sits comfortably in the midpoint of the guided range.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides NVIDIA's actual issued guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**

Historical practice: Public companies rarely revise forward guidance in the 6 days immediately preceding earnings announcements. The guidance range ($89.2B–$92.8B) already includes a 2% buffer on either side, which is a standard confidence band.

---

## Reasoning on the distribution

Given that:
1. Guidance was issued just ~3 months ago (May 20, 2026)
2. The earnings release is 6 days away
3. The guidance includes a standard ±2% buffer
4. Wall Street consensus falls within the guided range
5. No material negative news appears in the research

The probability distribution should be **heavily concentrated around the $91.0 billion midpoint**, with the tails extending modestly beyond the ±2% formal guidance range to account for small possibilities of last-minute revisions.

I estimate:
- **Median**: $91.0 billion (the stated midpoint)
- **10th percentile**: ~$88.5 billion (below the formal guidance floor, accounting for tail risk of unexpected downward revision)
- **90th percentile**: ~$93.5 billion (above the formal guidance ceiling, accounting for tail risk of unexpected upward revision)

Low (10th percentile): 88500000000
Median (50th percentile): 91000000000
High (90th percentile): 93500000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to report its Q2 FY227 earnings on August 26, 2026. For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's self-issued revenue guidance, announced on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance implies a range with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' consensus estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/) [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors).

The company's outlook explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/) [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance implies a significant year-over-year growth of about 94% compared to Q2 FY2026 revenue of $46.7 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors).
